report.summary: Chunk 7 of publish.py: publish_to_pr() with secret floor, gate, dry_run; read_pr_thread() reads PR comments; _parse_comment() stub.
risks: read_pr_thread: STAT_REFUSED_SECRET on pr/repo screen | medium | screen_egress for read may be overly broad; no evidence of data sent | check if screen_egress is intended for read operations in other files

handoff.purpose: Defines publish_to_pr() and read_pr_thread() functions with egress gating, dry-run support, and PR comment reading.

symbols.name: publish_to_pr
symbols.note: Renders verdict, runs egress gate, optionally spawns gh process (unless dry_run or gate hit). Returns PublishResult.

symbols.name: read_pr_thread
symbols.note: Reads PR comments via gh process, returns ThreadResult with turns. Includes egress gate on pr/repo.

symbols.name: _parse_comment
symbols.note: Private helper to convert a gh comment JSON object to PRTurn. Handles two author shapes.

claims.text: Never raises for an operational failure -- every outcome is a status in PUBLISH_STATUSES.
claims.why: The claim refers to PUBLISH_STATUSES which is not defined in this chunk; no exception handling is visible beyond return statements.

claims.text: dry_run=True renders and gates but does NOT invoke the runner at all; the markdown comes back on the result.
claims.why: Code: if dry_run: return PublishResult(status=STATUS_DRY_RUN, markdown=body, ...) after gate, before runner invocation.

claims.text: The gate still runs, so a dry run is an honest rehearsal rather than a way around the floor.
claims.why: Code: screen_egress is called before the dry_run check, so gate always runs.

claims.text: The body goes to gh on STDIN via --body-file -: a deliberation exceeds the Windows argv limit, and stdin keeps the payload inspectable by a fake runner in tests exactly as argv would be.
claims.why: The claim about the method of passing body (--body-file -) is not visible in this chunk; the actual invocation of gh is done by runner(argv, body) but argv is built by _gh_argv which is not shown.

claims.text: EGRESS GATE. Runs before the runner exists as far as this function is concerned -- on refusal we return without ever constructing a call.
claims.why: Code: screen_egress is called before any runner invocation; if hit returns early.

claims.text: The matched text is never echoed, and the markdown is withheld so a caller cannot log the refused body.
claims.why: Code: detail string does not include body; markdown is not included in the PublishResult for STATUS_REFUSED_SECRET.

claims.text: Never raises for an operational failure; every outcome is a status in READ_STATUSES.
claims.why: The claim refers to READ_STATUSES which is not defined in this chunk; no exception handling is visible beyond return statements.

claims.text: Nothing read here is authoritative: a reply is INPUT to a later round, not a verdict, and it is not on the hash-chained bus until the council appends it there.
claims.why: The claim refers to 'hash-chained bus' and council appending, which are concepts outside this chunk.

claims.text: One gh comment object -> one PRTurn. Tolerant of the two author shapes gh uses (author.login from the GraphQL-backed pr view --json, user.login from the REST-backed gh api).
claims.why: Code: author_obj = _field(raw, 'author', 'user', default=None); then checks if isinstance(author_obj, (str, bytes)). This handles both 'author' and 'user' keys.

observations.what: publish_to_pr uses screen_egress with a dict containing 'council comment body' key, but the body value is the rendered markdown which may contain sensitive data. The gate is applied before sending, matching the docstring.

read_pr_thread also applies screen_egress on the pr reference and repo slug, but this is a read operation; no data is being sent to GitHub (only metadata). This might be overly restrictive if screen_egress is intended for outgoing data only.

_parse_comment handles two possible keys ('author', 'user') but the fallback default=None means if neither exists, author_obj is None, and then isinstance(None, (str, bytes)) is False, leading to else branch which may fail if not handled. However, the code snippet ends before that branch.
